items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: they threw another curve at me... Marion Williams... they were making, it was strictly a Gospel album... Bill Fischer... he did like just some simple charts... I would just do it without thinking. I says, oh, boy, every time they had to do another take it was my fault.

ctx.x: You know you trade-off one thing for the other.

Yeah, you have to. Yes. Because when I was with, I think it was Atlantic Records, they threw another curve at me. It was this, oh what was her name, she was a gospel singer, Marion Williams, used to have a group called the Stars of Faith. And she was strictly out of the church. And so they were making, it was strictly a Gospel album. It wasn’t a jazz album you know. And so Bill Fischer, who is an arranger around town, a very good arranger too, he did like just some simple charts and outlines you know, like chord…
Oh, man, you should tape one of your fingers together.
